p.src: Grandmother Jia said, “That is exactly what I mean. I meant to say this last time, but I saw how many important matters you already had to manage, and now all these new troubles have arisen. Though you would never dare complain, you might well think that I care only for these young grandsons and granddaughters of mine and show no consideration for those of you who run the household. Since you have said it yourself, so much the better.” As Aunt Xue and Aunt Li were both present, and Lady Xing and You-shi with her daughters-in-law had also come to pay their respects and had not yet departed, Grandmother Jia said to Lady Wang and the others, “Only today have I spoken of this. Ordinarily I keep silent, first because I fear it might swell that girl Feng’s pride, and second because the others might not accept it. But today you are all here, and all of you have known what it is to deal with sisters-in-law and husbands’ sisters. Have you ever known anyone as thoughtful as she is?” Aunt Xue, Aunt Li, You-shi, and the others all laughed and said, “She truly is a rarity. Others show courtesy merely for appearance’s sake, but she genuinely cares for her younger brothers- and sisters-in-law. And toward you, Old Madam, she is truly filial as well.” Grandmother Jia nodded and sighed. “Fond as I am of her, I sometimes fear that being too quick-witted may not be a blessing.” Xifeng hastily replied with a laugh, “There you are mistaken, Old Ancestress. People say that those who are too clever and quick-witted are unlikely to live long. Anyone else may say it and anyone else may believe it, but you alone, Old Ancestress, ought neither to say nor believe such a thing. You are ten times cleverer and quicker-witted than I am, Old Ancestress, yet see how richly blessed you are with both longevity and good fortune! Perhaps one day I shall even surpass you twofold! After I have lived a thousand years, I shall wait until you have gone to the Western Paradise before I die.” Grandmother Jia laughed. “When everyone else is dead and only we two old goblins remain, what pleasure would there be in that?” At this, everyone burst out laughing.

p.src: Baoyu, preoccupied with Qingwen, Xiren, and the others, returned to the Garden ahead of everyone else. When he entered his room, the scent of medicine filled the air, but not another soul was in sight. Qingwen alone lay on the kang, her fevered face flaming scarlet. He touched her and found her burning hot. He quickly warmed his hands over the stove, then slipped one beneath the quilt to feel her body; it too was burning like fire. “Never mind that the others have gone,” he said, “but could Sheyue and Qiuwen be so heartless as to go off too?” Qingwen replied, “I sent Qiuwen away to have her meal, and Sheyue went out just now because Pinger came looking for her. The two of them were acting furtively; I have no idea what they are talking about. They must be saying that I am pretending to be ill so I need not go out.” “Pinger is not that sort of person,” said Baoyu. Besides, she did not know you were ill and could not have come especially to see you. She must have come to speak with Sheyue and, happening to find you ill, casually said that she had come to see how you were. It is quite natural for a tactful person to say something pleasing in such circumstances. Even if there were something wrong in your staying behind, what would it have to do with her? You have always been good friends; she would never damage your friendship over something that did not concern her.” “That is true,” said Qingwen. “I only wonder why she has suddenly begun keeping secrets from me.” Baoyu laughed. “Let me slip out through the back door and listen beneath the window to what they are saying. Then I will come back and tell you.” With that, he did indeed go out through the back door, creep beneath the window, and listen.

p.src: He heard Sheyue ask softly, “How did you come to recover it?” Pinger replied, “It disappeared that day while I was washing my hands. Second Mistress would not allow any commotion to be made, but as soon as she left the Garden, word was sent to the matrons in every part of it to investigate discreetly. We suspected Miss Xing’s maid. They are poor, after all, and we thought that an inexperienced young girl might well have picked it up. We never imagined it could have been someone from your quarters. Luckily, Second Mistress was not in her room when Nanny Song from your quarters arrived with the bracelet. She said she had seen the little maid Zhui’er steal it and had come to report the matter to Second Mistress. I hurriedly took the bracelet from her and thought it over: Baoyu takes particular care over all of you and prides himself on keeping his household above reproach. Yet only a year or two have passed since Liang’er stole the jade, and people still bring it up whenever it suits them; now another thief has appeared, this time stealing gold. And what is worse, she stole from a neighboring household. He, of all people, must suffer this, and one of his own servants must make a mockery of his claims. So I hastily warned Nanny Song not to tell Baoyu under any circumstances, but to act as though nothing had happened and not mention it to a soul. Secondly, the Old Madam and the Mistress would be angry if they heard of it. Thirdly, it would reflect badly on Xiren and all of you. So I told Second Mistress only this: ‘I was on my way to First Mistress’s quarters when the bracelet slipped from my wrist and fell among the grass roots. The snow was so deep that I did not see it. Today the snow had completely melted, and there it still lay, gleaming yellow in the sunlight, so I picked it up.’ Second Mistress believed me, and that is why I have come to tell you. From now on, keep an eye on the girl and do not send her on errands elsewhere. When Xiren returns, discuss it among yourselves and contrive some way of dismissing her. That will settle the matter.” Sheyue said, “That little wretch has seen her share of fine things. How can she be so grasping and shortsighted?” Pinger said, “How much could this bracelet weigh, after all? Second Mistress herself said that it is called a ‘shrimp-whisker bracelet’; only the pearl is of some value. That imp Qingwen is a piece of exploding charcoal; if she were told, she could never restrain herself. Once her temper flared, she would beat or curse the girl, and the whole affair would be noisily exposed after all. That is why I am telling only you, so that you can keep watch.” With that, she took her leave and departed.

p.src: When Baoyu heard this, he felt joy, anger, and sorrow all at once. He was glad that Ping’er had shown such consideration for him, angry at Zhui’er’s petty theft, and sorry that so clever a girl as Zhui’er should have done such a shameful thing. He therefore returned to his room and related Ping’er’s words to Qingwen in full detail. He added, “She said you were proud and strong-willed, and that hearing this while you were ill would only make you worse, so she meant to tell you after you recovered.” On hearing this, Qingwen’s arched brows drew sharply together and her phoenix eyes opened wide with fury; she immediately called for Zhui’er. Baoyu hurriedly dissuaded her. “If you raise an outcry now, won’t you be betraying Ping’er’s kindness toward us both? We had better accept her kindness and simply send the girl away afterward.” Qingwen said, “Even so, how can I possibly swallow this anger?” “What is there to be angry about?” said Baoyu. “Just concentrate on getting well.”

p.src: Qingwen took her medicine and another dose that evening. Although she perspired a little during the night, it had not yet taken effect: she still had a fever, a headache, a blocked nose, and a thick, congested voice. The next day Imperial Physician Wang came to examine her again and modified the prescription for her decoction. Though her fever subsided somewhat, her head still ached. Baoyu told Sheyue, “Bring the snuff. Let her inhale enough to provoke several hard sneezes, and that will clear the passages.” Sheyue duly fetched a flat glass box flecked with gold and fitted with a double gold clasp, and handed it to Baoyu. Baoyu flipped open the lid. Inside was a Western enamel picture of a naked, yellow-haired woman with fleshy wings growing from her sides, and the box contained genuine Wangqia foreign snuff. Qingwen was absorbed in looking at the picture, but Baoyu said, “Take a sniff. It will lose its strength if you leave it open.” At this, Qingwen hurriedly scooped up a little with her fingernail and sniffed it, but felt little effect. So she scooped up a much larger quantity and sniffed again. Suddenly, a sharp, sour sting shot through her nose to the crown of her head. She sneezed five or six times in succession, and tears and mucus instantly streamed together. Qingwen hurriedly closed the box and laughed. “Good heavens, how wonderfully relieving! Bring me some paper.” A young maid had already handed her a sheaf of fine paper, and Qingwen used the sheets one by one to clear her nose. “How is it?” Baoyu asked with a smile. Qingwen smiled. “It certainly feels clearer, but my temples still hurt.” Baoyu laughed. “We might as well treat you entirely with Western medicines; perhaps that will cure you.” Then he instructed Sheyue, “Go and ask Second Mistress Lian for some. Tell her I said that she often has that Western headache plaster called ‘Iphena.’ Ask her to find us a little.” Sheyue assented and went away. After quite some time she returned with half a strip of it. She found a scrap of red satin, cut out two circles the size of a fingertip, warmed and softened the medicine, and spread it on them with a hairpin. Holding a handled mirror herself, Qingwen stuck them over her two temples. Sheyue laughed. “You were as wild-haired as a sick ghost, but now that you have put those on, you look rather charming. Second Mistress Lian wears them so often that they hardly show on her.” After saying this, she turned to Baoyu. “Second Mistress Lian says that tomorrow is your uncle’s birthday, and Madam has said you are to attend. What will you wear tomorrow? We had better prepare everything tonight, so that there will be no fuss in the morning.” “Whatever comes readily to hand will do,” said Baoyu. “All year long there are so many birthday celebrations that one loses track of them.” With that, he rose, left the room, and went to Xichun’s quarters to see the painting.

p.src: Just as he reached the courtyard gate, he suddenly saw Baoqin’s young maid, Xiaoluo, passing by. Baoyu hurried after her and asked, “Where are you going?” Xiaoluo smiled. “Both our young ladies are in Miss Lin’s room. I’m on my way there now too.” Hearing this, Baoyu changed direction and accompanied her to the Xiaoxiang Lodge. Not only were the Baochai sisters there, but Xing Xiuyan was there as well; the four young ladies sat around the heated couch, chatting about family matters. Zijuan sat in the warm inner room, doing needlework by the window. When they saw him enter, they all laughed. “Here comes another one! But there is nowhere left for you to sit.” Baoyu laughed. “What a splendid ‘Gathering of Winter Beauties in a Lady’s Chamber’! What a pity I arrived a step too late. At any rate, this room is warmer than the others, and I shall not be cold sitting on this chair.” As he spoke, he sat down on the chair Daiyu usually used, which was draped with a gray-squirrel chair cover. In the warm inner room he noticed a long jade planter containing a cluster of single-petaled narcissi, ornamented with pieces of Xuan stone, and exclaimed in lavish praise, “What lovely flowers! The warmer this room grows, the purer the flowers’ fragrance becomes. They were not here yesterday.” Daiyu explained, “These came from Steward Lai’s wife, who sent Second Miss Xue two pots of winter-sweet and two pots of narcissi. She gave me one pot of narcissi, and she gave that girl Jiao one pot of winter-sweet. At first I did not want to accept it, but I was afraid of disappointing her good intentions. If you want it, how about letting me pass it on to you?” Baoyu replied, “I do have two pots in my room, but they are not as fine as this one. But since Cousin Baoqin gave it to you, how could you pass it on to someone else? That would never do.” Daiyu said, “My medicine kettle never leaves the fire all day long; I am practically nourished on medicine. How could I bear to have flower fragrance filling the room as well? It would only make me weaker. Besides, the medicinal smell in this room only spoils the flowers’ fragrance by mingling with it. You had better carry it away. Then the flowers too will be left pure and undisturbed by other smells.” Baoyu laughed. “There is someone ill in my room today, and medicine is being brewed there too. How did you know?” Daiyu laughed. “What a strange thing to say! I spoke without any particular intention. How should I know what goes on in your room? You did not come earlier to hear the old tales, and now that you have finally arrived, you take innocent remarks personally and make a fuss over them.”

p.src: Baoyu laughed. “Now we have a theme for our next poetry gathering tomorrow: we can write on narcissus and wintersweet.” Daiyu laughed when she heard this. “Enough, enough! I shall never dare write another poem. Every time I do, I am punished; it is mortifying for no reason at all.” As she spoke, she covered her face with both hands. Baoyu laughed. “Why must you do that? Why mock me again? Even I am not ashamed, yet there you are hiding your face.” Baochai laughed. “Next time I shall host a gathering, with four poetry themes and four lyric themes. Each person must compose four poems and four lyrics. The first poetry theme will be ‘Ode to the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate’: a regulated five-character verse using the xian rhyme category, and every rhyme in that category must be exhausted without leaving a single one unused.” Baoqin laughed. “That proves you are not sincere about founding a poetry club, sister. You are plainly trying to make things difficult for us. Strictly speaking, one could force something out, but it would amount to dragging in phrases from the Book of Changes and rearranging them this way and that. What pleasure could there be in that? When I was eight, I went with my father to the shores of the Western Sea to buy foreign goods. There we happened to see a girl from the Land of Zhenzhen, only fifteen years old. Her face was like that of a beauty in a Western painting. Her yellow hair hung in linked tresses, and her head was covered with coral, cat’s-eyes, emeralds, and other jewels. She wore sleeves of foreign brocade woven with gold thread like chain mail, and carried a Japanese sword likewise inlaid with gold and gems. Truly, even the beauties in paintings were not as lovely as she. Someone said that she was versed in Chinese poetry and literature, could expound the Five Classics, and knew how to compose both verse and lyrics. My father therefore prevailed upon an interpreter to ask her for a piece of calligraphy, and what she wrote was a poem of her own composition.” Everyone marvelled at this extraordinary tale. Baoyu hastily said with a smile, “Dear sister, bring it out and let me see it.” Baoqin laughed. “It is stored away in Nanjing. How could I fetch it now?” Baoyu was bitterly disappointed and said, “I have not been blessed with the fortune to see such a wonder.” Daiyu laughingly took Baoqin by the hand. “Do not try to fool us. I know that when you came here, you would hardly have left such things at home; naturally you must have brought them with you. Now you are lying and saying you did not. The others may believe you, but I do not.” Baoqin blushed, lowered her head, and smiled without speaking. Baochai laughed. “This Pin’er is forever saying such needless things, just to show how clever she is.” Daiyu said, “If you brought it, you might as well let us broaden our horizons.” Baochai laughed. “There is a great heap of trunks and cases that has not yet been sorted. Who knows which one it is in? Once everything has been put in order in a few days, we can find it and all look at it together.”

The others may believe you, but I do not.”
Baoqin blushed, lowered her head, and smiled without speaking.
Baochai laughed. “This Pin’er is forever saying such needless things, just to show how clever she is.”
Daiyu said, “If you brought it, you might as well let us broaden our horizons.”
Baochai laughed. “There is a great heap of trunks and cases that has not yet been sorted. Who knows which one it is in?
Once everything has been put in order in a few days, we can find it and all look at it together.”

p.src: Then she said to Baoqin, “If you remember it, why not recite it for us?” Only then did Baoqin reply, “I remember it was a regulated five-character poem. For a foreign girl, it was quite an achievement.” Baochai said, “Do not recite it yet. Wait until we have called Yun’er over, so that she may hear it too.” With that, she summoned Xiaoluo and instructed her, “Go to my rooms and say that a foreign beauty has come here who writes excellent poetry. Ask that ‘poetry madwoman’ to come and see her, and bring our ‘poetry simpleton’ along as well.” Xiaoluo went off laughing.

p.src: When they had heard it, everyone exclaimed, “What an achievement for her! She is actually better than we Chinese are.” Before they had finished speaking, Sheyue came in and said, “Her Ladyship has sent someone to tell Second Master that you are to go to your uncle’s first thing tomorrow morning and say that she is rather unwell and cannot come in person.” Baoyu hurriedly rose and answered, “Yes.” He then asked whether Baochai and Baoqin would be going. Baochai said, “We are not going. We sent our gifts separately yesterday.” After chatting a while longer, everyone dispersed.

p.src: Baoyu let all his girl cousins go ahead and himself remained behind. Daiyu called him back again and asked, “When exactly will Xiren return?” Baoyu replied, “Naturally, not until the funeral procession is over.” Daiyu had more to say, but the words never left her lips. After staring abstractedly for a while, she said, “You had better go.” Baoyu too felt that he had many things in his heart, yet he did not know what to say. After thinking for a moment, he smiled and said, “Let us talk tomorrow.” He stepped down from the stone threshold and was just about to move on with lowered head when he hurriedly turned back and asked, “The nights are growing longer now. How many times do you cough during the night? How often do you wake?” Daiyu said, “Last night was better. I coughed only twice, but I slept for merely one watch after the fourth watch began, and then could not sleep again.” Baoyu smiled again. “There was indeed something important I meant to tell you; I have only just remembered it.” As he spoke, he moved closer and whispered, “I was thinking about the bird’s-nest Baochai gave you—” Before he could finish, Concubine Zhao came in to visit Daiyu and asked, “Have you been well these past two days, miss?” Daiyu knew that she had come from Tanchun’s quarters and, happening to pass her door, had stopped in as a matter of courtesy. Daiyu hastily smiled, offered her a seat, and said, “How kind of you to think of me, aunt. It is bitterly cold, yet you have come all this way yourself.” She hurriedly ordered tea to be served, while at the same time signalling to Baoyu with her eyes. Baoyu understood and went out.

p.src: It was just suppertime when he went to see Lady Wang, who again urged him to set out early. When Baoyu returned, he watched Qingwen take her medicine. That night Baoyu did not have Qingwen moved out of the warm chamber, but slept outside it himself. He also ordered the brazier-cage moved in front of the warm chamber, and Sheyue slept on it. The night passed without incident. Before dawn the next day, Qingwen woke Sheyue and said, “You ought to wake up too—you can never get enough sleep! Go out and have someone prepare his tea and hot water; I’ll wake him.” Sheyue hurriedly threw on her clothes and rose, saying, “Let’s wake him, get him dressed, and move him over beyond this heated chest before we call the others in. The old nurses have already said he shouldn’t stay in this room, for fear he might catch your illness. If they see the three of us crowded together now, they’ll start nagging again.” “That’s just what I was thinking,” said Qingwen. Just as the two were about to call him, Baoyu woke and hurriedly sat up to put on his clothes. Sheyue first called in the little maids to set everything in order; only then did she summon Qiuwen, Tanyun, and the others, who together helped Baoyu finish washing and dressing. Sheyue said, “The sky is overcast again, and I’m afraid it may snow. You’d better wear that felt outfit.” Baoyu nodded and changed at once. A little maid brought a covered bowl of lotus-seed and red-date soup on a small tea tray, and Baoyu took two sips. Sheyue then offered him a small dish of specially prepared purple ginger, and Baoyu held a piece in his mouth. After giving Qingwen a few more instructions, he went to Grandmother Jia’s quarters.

p.src: Grandmother Jia had not yet risen, but when she learned that Baoyu was going out, she had the door opened and told him to come in. Baoyu saw that Baoqin was asleep behind Grandmother Jia, facing inward, and had not yet woken. Grandmother Jia saw that Baoyu was wearing a lychee-colored Russian-wool riding jacket with arrow sleeves, and over it a crimson felt tasselled coat embroidered in gold and colors and edged with dark-blue figured satin. “Is it snowing?” Grandmother Jia asked. “It’s overcast, but it hasn’t begun to snow yet,” Baoyu replied. Grandmother Jia then called for Yuanyang. “Give him that black-cloud leopard cloak from yesterday.” Yuanyang acknowledged the order, went away, and duly brought back a cloak. When Baoyu looked at it, it glittered magnificently with gold, kingfisher-blue, and flashes of emerald, yet it was unlike the duck-down cape Baoqin wore. Grandmother Jia laughed. “This is called ‘peacock-gold wool.’ It was woven in Russia from thread spun with peacock feathers. The other day I gave that wild-duck one to your little cousin; you may have this one.” Baoyu kowtowed once and put it around his shoulders. Grandmother Jia laughed. “Go and show it to your mother before you leave.” Baoyu agreed and came out, only to see Yuanyang standing there rubbing her eyes. Ever since the day Yuanyang had sworn her irrevocable oath, she had never spoken to Baoyu. Baoyu had been uneasy about it day and night; now, seeing that she meant to avoid him again, he went up to her and said with a smile, “Dear sister, look—does this suit me?” Yuanyang jerked her hand away and went straight into Grandmother Jia’s room. Baoyu had no choice but to go to Lady Wang’s room and show it to her. He then returned to the Garden and showed it to Qingwen and Sheyue before going back to Grandmother Jia’s room to report, “Mother saw it and only said it was far too precious. She told me to wear it carefully and not spoil it.” “This is the only one left,” said Grandmother Jia. “If you spoil it, there will be no other. And having another made especially for you now is out of the question.” Then she cautioned him again, “Don’t drink too much wine, and come home early.” Baoyu answered “Yes” several times.

p.src: An old nurse followed him to the main hall. There she found Baoyu’s foster-brother Li Gui together with Wang Rong, Zhang Ruojin, Zhao Yihua, Qian Qi, and Zhou Rui. They had brought four young pages—Mingyan, Banhe, Chuyao, and Saohong—who carried clothes bundles and seat cushions, while a white horse with a carved saddle and colored bridle stood ready; they had all been waiting for some time. The old nurse gave the six men a few more instructions. They hastily answered “Yes” several times, then presented the whip and held down the stirrup. Baoyu slowly mounted. Li Gui and Wang Rong held the bit-rings, Qian Qi and Zhou Rui led the way, and Zhang Ruojin and Zhao Yihua kept close behind Baoyu on either side. From horseback Baoyu said with a smile, “Brother Zhou, Brother Qian, let’s go out through this side gate. Then I won’t have to dismount again when we reach Father’s study.” Zhou Rui turned sideways and replied with a smile, “Master is away, and the study is kept locked every day. Surely you needn’t dismount, young master.” Baoyu laughed. “Even if it is locked, I must still dismount.” Qian Qi, Li Gui, and the others all laughed. “You are quite right, young master. If you were to take it easy and not dismount, and happened to meet Steward Lai or Second Master Lin, they might not presume to rebuke you, but they would still offer a word or two of advice. Then every fault would be laid at our door, and they would say we had failed to teach you proper manners.” Zhou Rui and Qian Qi then led the way straight out through the side gate.

p.src: While they were still speaking, they saw Lai Da coming toward them, just as expected. Baoyu quickly reined in his horse and made to dismount. Lai Da hurried forward and caught hold of his leg to stop him. Baoyu stood up in the stirrups, took Lai Da’s hand with a smile, and exchanged a few words with him. Next they saw a young servant leading in twenty or thirty men carrying brooms and dustpans. At the sight of Baoyu, they all stood respectfully along the wall with their hands lowered; only the servant at their head knelt on one knee and offered a formal greeting. Baoyu did not know his name, so he merely smiled and nodded. Only after the horse had passed did the servant lead his men away. They then passed through the side gate. Outside, the personal servants of Li Gui and the other five men, together with several grooms, had already prepared more than ten horses and were waiting especially for them. As soon as they were through the gate, Li Gui and the others each mounted, and with some leading ahead and others surrounding Baoyu, the whole party swept away in a cloud of dust. Nothing more need be said of their journey.

p.src: After taking her medicine, Qingwen still showed no improvement. In her impatience she cursed the doctor: “All he knows is how to cheat people out of their money. He cannot even give me one dose of decent medicine.” Sheyue laughed and tried to soothe her: “You are far too impatient. As the saying goes, ‘Illness comes like a collapsing mountain but departs like silk drawn from a cocoon.’ It is not the Lord Lao’s elixir of immortality; how could any medicine work so miraculously? Just rest quietly for a few days and you will naturally recover. The more anxious you become, the more stubborn the illness will be.” Qingwen then berated the little maids: “Where have you all burrowed away to? The moment you saw that I was ill, you all grew bold enough to run off. Once I am well tomorrow, I shall skin every last one of you!” Terrified, the little maid Zhuan’er hurried in and asked, “What do you need, miss?” Qingwen said, “Have all the others dropped dead, then, leaving only you?” As she spoke, Zhui’er came sidling in as well. Qingwen said, “Just look at this little wretch! She would not have come at all if no one had called her. When monthly allowances are handed out or fruit is distributed, you are always the first to come running. Come closer. I am not a tiger that will eat you!” Zhui’er had no choice but to edge forward. Qingwen suddenly raised herself and seized Zhui’er’s hand. Taking a long hairpin from beside her pillow, she jabbed it wildly into the girl’s hand and cursed: “What use are these claws of yours? They cannot hold a needle or manage a thread; all they can do is steal food. You are greedy and light-fingered, a shameless disgrace. They would be better stabbed to pieces!” Zhui’er screamed and wept in pain. Sheyue hastily pulled Zhui’er away and pressed Qingwen back onto the bed. Laughing, she said, “You have only just broken into a sweat, and now you are trying to kill yourself again. Once you are well, you may beat her as much as you please. Why make such a commotion now?” Qingwen ordered someone to summon Nanny Song and said, “Second Master Bao told me just now to tell you that Zhui’er is extremely lazy. When he gives her an order to her face, she will not even stir her lips in reply; and when Xiren orders her about, she curses her behind her back. She must be sent away today without fail. Tomorrow Second Master Bao will explain the matter to madam himself.” On hearing this, Nanny Song understood that the affair of the bracelet had come to light. She smiled and said, “Even so, we ought to wait until Miss Hua returns and is informed before sending her away.” Qingwen said, “Second Master Bao charged me over and over again today. Never mind ‘Miss Hua’ or ‘Miss Grass’; we have our reasons. Just do as I say and quickly summon her family to take her away.” Sheyue said, “That will do. She must leave sooner or later, and if she is taken away now, we shall have one extra day of peace.”

p.src: Having heard this, Nanny Song had no choice but to go out and summon Zhui’er’s mother. After the girl’s belongings had been packed, the woman came to see Qingwen and the others and said, “What is the matter with you young ladies? If your niece has misbehaved, you should correct her. Why drive her out? At least spare us some dignity.” Qingwen said, “Save that question for Baoyu when he returns. It has nothing to do with us.” The woman sneered. “As if I would dare go and question him! Is there anything he does that is not settled according to you young ladies’ wishes? Even if he agreed, it would be no use if you young ladies refused. Why, only a moment ago, though speaking in private, you called him directly by name. When you young ladies do that it is acceptable, but if we did it we would be condemned as uncouth savages.” At this Qingwen grew still more incensed, and her face flushed red. “Yes, I called him by name. Go and report me to the Old Lady. Tell her I behaved outrageously, and have me driven out as well.” Sheyue hurriedly said, “Sister-in-law, just take the girl away for now. Anything else can be discussed later. Is this a place where you may shout and lecture us about propriety? Have you ever seen anyone insist on formalities with us? Not only you—even Granny Lai and Matron Lin must make allowances for us. As for calling him by name, from his childhood until now it has always been done at the Old Lady’s own instruction. You all know that, fearing he might be difficult to rear, she deliberately had his childhood name written down and posted everywhere so that thousands of people would call him by it, all to help him grow up safely. Even water carriers, night-soil carriers, and beggars may call him by it—how much more may we! Why, only yesterday Matron Lin called him ‘Master,’ and the Old Lady reproved her for it. That is one reason. Secondly, we are constantly reporting matters to the Old Lady. If we cannot use his name when we speak, must we call him ‘Master’ instead? There is not a day when we do not say the name Baoyu two hundred times, yet you choose to find fault with this! When you have time one day, listen to us in the presence of the Old Lady and madam; then you will hear us call him by name to his face and understand. You have never held a respectable post in attendance upon the Old Lady or madam, but spend the whole year loitering outside the inner gate. No wonder you do not know the rules within these apartments. This is no place for you to linger. If you remain a little longer, someone will come and question you without our needing to say a word. If you have any grievance to argue, take her away for now, report it to Matron Lin, and ask her to come and speak to the Second Master. There are more than a thousand people in this household. If first you and then another came rushing in, we could not possibly keep straight who everyone was, much less learn all their names!” With that, she called to a little maid, “Bring the floor cloth and wipe the floor!” The woman had no answer. Not daring to remain any longer, she angrily took Zhui’er and left.

At this Qingwen grew still more incensed, and her face flushed red. “Yes, I called him by name. Go and report me to the Old Lady. Tell her I behaved outrageously, and have me driven out as well.”
Sheyue hurriedly said, “Sister-in-law, just take the girl away for now. Anything else can be discussed later.
Is this a place where you may shout and lecture us about propriety?
Have you ever seen anyone insist on formalities with us?
Not only you—even Granny Lai and Matron Lin must make allowances for us.

As for calling him by name, from his childhood until now it has always been done at the Old Lady’s own instruction. You all know that, fearing he might be difficult to rear, she deliberately had his childhood name written down and posted everywhere so that thousands of people would call him by it, all to help him grow up safely.
Even water carriers, night-soil carriers, and beggars may call him by it—how much more may we!
Why, only yesterday Matron Lin called him ‘Master,’ and the Old Lady reproved her for it. That is one reason.
Secondly, we are constantly reporting matters to the Old Lady. If we cannot use his name when we speak, must we call him ‘Master’ instead?
There is not a day when we do not say the name Baoyu two hundred times, yet you choose to find fault with this!
When you have time one day, listen to us in the presence of the Old Lady and madam; then you will hear us call him by name to his face and understand.

You have never held a respectable post in attendance upon the Old Lady or madam, but spend the whole year loitering outside the inner gate. No wonder you do not know the rules within these apartments.
This is no place for you to linger. If you remain a little longer, someone will come and question you without our needing to say a word.
If you have any grievance to argue, take her away for now, report it to Matron Lin, and ask her to come and speak to the Second Master.
There are more than a thousand people in this household. If first you and then another came rushing in, we could not possibly keep straight who everyone was, much less learn all their names!”
With that, she called to a little maid, “Bring the floor cloth and wipe the floor!”
The woman had no answer. Not daring to remain any longer, she angrily took Zhui’er and left.

p.src: Nanny Song hurriedly said, “No wonder you do not know the rules, sister-in-law. Your daughter has served in this room, so before she leaves she ought at least to kowtow to the young ladies. You have no other parting gift to offer—and even if you did, they would not care for it—so she should at least kowtow to show her gratitude. How can you simply turn around and leave?” Hearing this, Zhui’er had no choice but to turn back. She came inside and kowtowed twice to the two of them, then went in search of Qiuwen and the others. They paid no attention to her. Her mother could only sigh and groan. Not daring to speak, she departed with resentment in her heart.

p.src: Qingwen had just caught another chill and grown upset, which made her feel even worse. She tossed and turned until the lamps were lit and had only just settled down a little. Just then Baoyu returned, sighing and stamping his feet the moment he entered. Sheyue hurriedly asked what had happened. Baoyu said, “Grandmother was so pleased when she gave me this coat today, but somehow the back hem got scorched. Luckily it was already dark, so neither Grandmother nor Mother noticed.” As he spoke, he took it off. When Sheyue examined it, she indeed found a hole as large as a fingertip. “A spark must have flown out of a hand warmer,” she said. “It is nothing serious. We should have someone take it out quietly at once and ask a skilled invisible-mender to repair it.” With that, she wrapped it in a bundle and gave it to an old serving woman to take out. “It must be ready by daybreak,” she said. “Whatever you do, do not let Grandmother or Mother find out.” The woman was gone a long while but eventually brought it back. “Not only the skilled invisible-menders,” she said, “but all the tailors, embroiderers, and needlewomen I asked failed even to recognize the material, and none dared undertake the job.” “What are we to do now?” exclaimed Sheyue. “Perhaps you had better simply not wear it tomorrow.” Baoyu said, “Tomorrow is the proper day of the celebration. Grandmother and Mother told me expressly to wear this.” “Would it not spoil everyone’s pleasure that I burned it just the day before?” Qingwen had been listening for some time. Unable to restrain herself, she turned over and said, “Bring it here and let me see.” “If you are not blessed enough to wear it, then let it be.” “Why become anxious about it now?” “You are quite right,” Baoyu replied with a smile. As he spoke, he handed it to Qingwen, moved the lamp closer, and examined it carefully with her for a while. Qingwen said, “This is woven with peacock-gold thread. If we use peacock-gold thread ourselves and darn the hole closely as though laying boundary stitches, we may be able to pass it off.” Sheyue laughed. “We have peacock thread ready at hand, but apart from you, who here knows how to make those boundary stitches?” “There is no help for it,” said Qingwen. “I shall risk my life over it.” Baoyu hastily protested, “How could I possibly allow that?” “You have only just improved a little. How can you possibly work?” “There is no need for you to make such a fuss,” said Qingwen. “I know my own condition.” As she spoke, she sat up, gathered her hair, and put on a garment. But her head felt heavy and her body weightless, while golden sparks danced wildly before her eyes; she truly could scarcely hold herself upright. Yet if she did not mend it, Baoyu would remain distressed, so she had no choice but to steel herself, grit her teeth, and endure. She told Sheyue merely to help by handling the thread. Qingwen first held up a strand for comparison and said with a smile, “It is not a perfect match, but once the hole is mended, it should not be very noticeable.” “That will do very well,” said Baoyu. “Where could we possibly find a tailor from Russia now?”

p.src: Qingwen first unpicked the lining and secured a bamboo embroidery hoop, about as wide as the mouth of a teacup, behind the damaged place. She then used gold scissors to fray and loosen the edges of the hole, after which she laid two threads with her needle to mark out warp and weft. Following the boundary-stitch method, she first formed the ground and then darned back and forth according to the pattern of the original cloth. After every two stitches she looked at it; after every two more, she examined it closely again. But her head spun, her sight darkened, her breath came short, and her strength failed. Before she had made even three or five stitches, she had to lean over the pillow and rest awhile. At her side, Baoyu would ask one moment, “Would you like some hot water?” The next moment he would urge, “Rest awhile.” Then he would take a gray-squirrel cloak and drape it over her shoulders, or have a bolster brought for her to lean against. Driven to distraction, Qingwen pleaded, “Dear little master!” “Please just go to sleep.” “If you stay up another half the night, your eyes will be hollowed out tomorrow. What shall we do then?” Seeing that she was becoming agitated, Baoyu had no choice but to lie down as best he could, though he still could not sleep. Presently the chiming clock struck four. Qingwen had only just finished the repair; she then used a little toothbrush to tease the nap out slowly. “This is very good,” said Sheyue. “Unless one looks closely, one cannot tell at all.” Baoyu hurriedly asked to see it and said, “It truly looks exactly the same.” Qingwen had already suffered several fits of coughing. Having completed the repair with great difficulty, she managed to say, “Mended it may be, but it still does not truly match. I cannot do another stitch!” With a cry of pain, she collapsed helplessly. To learn what followed, listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
